record_under_review.evidence_span: The study analyzes LLM weight entropy from 1.5B to 405B parameter models across bf16, int4, AWQ, and SQ8 formats, finding effective entropy 2–10x lower than stored bitwidth and theoretical footprint reduction up to 10x without changing weight values. It introduces tile-level on-the-fly lossless decompression using Asymmetric Numeral Systems aligned with GPU GEMM tiling. The system reaches within 0.01–0.1 bits of the Shannon limit, raises Qwen-14B maximum batch size from 47 to 75, improves Mixtral-176B batch size from 20 to 95, and reports up to 1.2x/1.6x throughput gains plus up to 11x over NeuZip and DFloat11.
record_under_review.hardware_or_process_assumptions: GPU inference with tile-level decompression integrated into SGLang and multi-GPU serving; exact decompression hardware/software cost, memory bandwidth, GPU models, and quality invariance conditions require full-paper verification.
record_under_review.limits: The evidence is an author preprint abstract; exact compression/decompression latency, CPU/GPU overhead, memory-bandwidth accounting, model-quality invariance, sequence lengths, and hardware implementation details require full-paper verification.
record_under_review.method_or_artifact: Entropy analysis across model sizes and numeric formats, followed by tile-level Asymmetric Numeral Systems compression and on-the-fly decompression aligned to GPU GEMM tiling, integrated with SGLang and multi-GPU serving.
metrics: up to 11x throughput improvement over NeuZip and DFloat11
record_under_review.problem: Trillion-parameter LLM weights can exceed GPU memory capacity, while conventional stored bitwidth overstates the intrinsic randomness of weights and lossless compression has not been tightly integrated with inference execution.
record_under_review.title: Approaching Shannon Bound with Lossless LLM Weight Compression
record_under_review.workload_or_benchmark: LLM serving across 1.5B–405B parameter models and bf16/int4/AWQ/SQ8 formats, including Qwen-14B and Mixtral-176B batch-size and throughput evaluation; comparisons include NeuZip and DFloat11.
